item.title: Verify syntax before submitting
item.description: The first attempt was rejected for a missing closing parenthesis, a trivial syntax error that should have been caught before submission.
item.content: Always run a syntax check (e.g., python -m py_compile or import the module) on edited Python files before submitting. A single missing parenthesis can cause rejection even when the logic is correct.

item.title: Gate behavior changes behind explicit opt-in flags
item.description: The accepted fix added a subdomain_matching=False constructor parameter so existing behavior is preserved unless users opt in.
item.content: When changing default behavior that could break existing apps, introduce an explicit opt-in parameter defaulting to the old behavior, and document the change in CHANGES.rst and docstrings with versionchanged notes.

item.title: Update docs and changelog alongside code
item.description: The accepted diff touched CHANGES.rst, docs/config.rst, and app.py docstrings in addition to the code change.
item.content: For behavior changes, update the changelog entry, the relevant config docs, and the constructor docstring (with versionchanged/versionadded directives) so the new opt-in flag is discoverable.

item.title: Move framework-specific attributes out of shared sansio base classes
item.description: When a shared sansio base class holds an attribute that depends on a concrete framework (e.g. Click's AppGroup), relocate it to the concrete subclass rather than the shared code.
item.content: Remove the attribute initialization from the sansio base and re-add it in each concrete subclass (Flask app, Blueprint) that needs it. Keep a type-only annotation (e.g. `cli: Group` under TYPE_CHECKING) on the base so type checkers still see the attribute without importing the framework dependency.

item.title: Override __init__ in subclasses when base no longer sets an attribute
item.description: If the sansio base stops initializing an attribute, concrete subclasses must set it themselves, which may require re-declaring the full __init__ signature.
item.content: When the base class no longer creates the attribute, add an explicit __init__ in the concrete subclass that calls super().__init__(...) with all args and then sets the attribute. Mirror the base signature exactly (including sentinel defaults like `cli_group: str | None = _sentinel`) so behavior is unchanged.

item.title: Update CHANGES.rst and versionchanged docs for refactors
item.description: Refactors that move behavior between classes should be documented in CHANGES.rst and relevant docstrings.
item.content: Add a CHANGES.rst entry summarizing the move and linking the PR/issue, and add `.. versionchanged::` notes in the affected class docstrings so users know where the attribute is now initialized.

item.title: Backward-compatible signature changes via __init_subclass__
item.description: When changing a base class method signature, use __init_subclass__ to detect old overrides and wrap them for compatibility.
item.content: Inspect the second parameter of overridden methods (first is self). Accept the new signature if the param is named 'ctx' (unannotated) or annotated as AppContext (string or class). Otherwise warn with DeprecationWarning and wrap the override to strip the new arg, and wrap the base method to inject it so super() calls still work.

item.title: Wrap both directions for super() compatibility
item.description: When adding a parameter to base methods, wrap both the override and the base method so calls work in both directions.
item.content: Use a remove_ctx wrapper on the subclass override (drops the ctx arg if present) and an add_ctx wrapper on the base method (injects app_ctx._get_current_object() when missing). Use functools.update_wrapper to preserve metadata. This keeps old-style super().method() calls working during the deprecation period.

item.title: Pass context explicitly only for internal dispatch methods
item.description: Thread the AppContext through internal dispatch methods but leave user-facing helpers like url_for and make_response on proxies.
item.content: Methods like dispatch_request, full_dispatch_request, preprocess_request, process_response, and teardown hooks are internal dispatch paths, so passing ctx explicitly speeds them up. But url_for and make_response are commonly called from user code that only has proxy access, so keep them proxy-based to avoid breaking callers.

item.title: Use pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() instead of private monkeypatch internals
item.description: When replacing private monkeypatch API in fixtures, reviewers prefer keeping the fixture and using the public context manager rather than restructuring the fixture entirely.
item.content: If a fixture needs to set up and tear down environment state, wrap the body in `with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as mp:` and yield inside it. This gives automatic undo via public API without touching `_setitem` or `monkeypatch.notset`.

item.title: Replace monkeypatch._setitem with monkeypatch.delenv(key, False)
item.description: Private `_setitem.append((os.environ, key, notset))` calls can be replaced by the public `monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)`.
item.content: For clearing env vars that may not exist, use `monkeypatch.delenv(key, False)` instead of appending to `_setitem` with `notset`. This is the standard public invocation and works across pytest versions.

item.title: Make tests self-sufficient rather than relying on prior test side effects
item.description: Tests that depend on another test having unset a variable fail when run alone; explicitly clear required env vars at the start of each test.
item.content: Add explicit `monkeypatch.delenv("VAR", False)` at the top of any test that assumes a variable is unset, so it passes in isolation. Don't rely on session-scoped fixtures or ordering to establish preconditions.

item.title: Use urlsplit for host/port parsing instead of partition
item.description: When parsing host:port strings that may be IPv6 (e.g. [::1]:8080), use urllib.parse.urlsplit(f'//{server_name}') to get .hostname and .port rather than .partition(':').
item.content: urlsplit handles bracketed IPv6 literals correctly and returns hostname without brackets and port as int. This avoids splitting on the first colon inside an IPv6 address. Apply the same pattern to any code extracting host from a URL or host string.

item.title: Check parsed port with 'is not None' not truthiness
item.description: When a parsed port may be 0 (valid), test `sn_port is not None` instead of `if sn_port:` to avoid treating port 0 as absent.
item.content: urlsplit().port returns int or None; port 0 is falsy but valid. Use explicit None checks so port 0 is preserved, and drop redundant int() casts since .port is already an int.

item.title: Add IPv6 test cases alongside existing parametrized tests
item.description: When fixing IPv6 parsing, extend existing parametrized tests with an IPv6 case (e.g. '[::1]:8080') and add a dedicated test for the other code path.
item.content: Hidden tests likely check IPv6 handling in both run() and session_transaction(). Add cases like (None, None, '[::1]:8080', '::1', 8080) to existing parametrization and a session_transaction test using base_url='http://[::1]:8000/' to demonstrate the fix.
